why_angle: printingxyz, 3dprinterlab and itechguides give no measured noise for any of these printers. They quote the maker's ratings, such as the A1 mini's '≤48 dB' or the 5M Pro's 50/55 dB, or say nothing about noise. This page puts four measurements from named reviewers side by side: Notebookcheck, Igor's Lab twice and 3DPrint.com. It shows that the enclosed 5M Pro measured a 68 dB average against its 50–55 dB rating, while the enclosed Centauri Carbon 2 measured 44–47 dB. That changes which enclosed printer belongs in a child's room.

page.title: Best 3D printer for kids and teens (2026): safe, easy picks and what parents run into
page.h1: Best 3D printer for kids and teens (2026)
page.desc: Measured noise for kid-friendly 3D printers. The enclosed Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 tested at 44–47 dB, the open Bambu A1 mini at 55.3 dB(A) and the Flashforge 5M Pro at 68 dB. Toybox is the pick for younger kids.
page.answer: Short answer. The best 3D printer for kids in 2026 is an enclosed PLA printer: the Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 measured 44–47 dB on average (Notebookcheck); Igor's Lab measured the open Bambu A1 mini at 55.3 dB(A). Younger kids: Toybox. Flashforge's 5M Pro adds a HEPA filter.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Room for bigger projects: the Centauri Carbon 2 builds 256 × 256 × 256 mm = 16.8 L, the 5M Pro 220 × 220 × 220 mm = 10.6 L and the A1 mini 180 × 180 × 180 mm = 5.83 L. So the CC2 has 16.8 ÷ 5.83 = 2.9 times the A1 mini's space.
  • Rated against measured: the 5M Pro is rated 50–55 dB depending on mode. 3DPrint.com measured a 68 dB average, so 68 − 55 = 13 dB to 68 − 50 = 18 dB above the rating. Elegoo claims 45 dB for the CC2, and Notebookcheck's 44–47 dB average sits right around it.
  • Enclosing the open Adventurer 5M: $249 + $39.99 for Flashforge's enclosure kit = $288.99, and Igor's Lab still measured it at 62.3 dB(A) while printing.
  • Toybox bundles: the Alpha Four Starter is $249 and the Pro Saver is $199. The $249 − $199 = $50 difference is a Toybox Pro membership that keeps billing until you cancel it.
  • Toybox build size: 75 × 80 × 90 mm = 0.54 L, against 5.83 L on the A1 mini (5.83 ÷ 0.54 = 10.8 times).
UseFitsWhy
Tween or teen printing in their own roomElegoo Centauri Carbon 2Enclosed, with the lowest measured average here (44–47 dB, Notebookcheck)
Parents who want fumes filteredFlashforge Adventurer 5M ProEnclosed, with a HEPA + carbon filter. Flashforge says it removes 99% of particles and VOCs, and no lab has tested that. Use its low-noise mode.
Younger child, first printerToybox Alpha Four (Starter bundle)Unheated print bed and a toy catalog of 25,000+ models (Toybox)
Shared desk with an adult nearbyBambu Lab A1 miniSmall and quieter than the open Adventurer 5M in Igor's Lab tests, but its 80 °C bed moves in the open

Measured noise against the number on the box

Every maker here quotes a best-case figure. Bambu says the A1 mini gets below 48 dB by sending high-frequency movements to its motors to cancel noise (Notebookcheck's launch report). Flashforge rates the 5M Pro at 50–55 dB depending on the mode you pick (3Dnatives). Elegoo claims 45 dB for the Centauri Carbon 2.

Named reviewers measured something else. Igor's Lab (Tim Kutzner) measured the A1 mini at 55.3 dB(A) from about 40 cm while printing. 3DPrint.com (Orville Wright IV) measured the enclosed 5M Pro at a 68 dB average, with a 79 dB maximum and a 46 dB minimum. He added that it went above 70 dB only for fractions of a second. Notebookcheck (Vineet Washington) measured the CC2 at 44–47 dB on average with peaks up to 54 dB. Igor's Lab put the open Adventurer 5M at 62.3 dB(A) printing and 41.1 dB(A) idle, mostly from its small hotend fan.

These are four tests with different setups. Only Igor's Lab gave a distance for the A1 mini, and 3DPrint.com and Notebookcheck gave none. Read the figures as a ranking, not exact gaps. An enclosure alone doesn't make a printer quiet: the 5M Pro is enclosed and still measured the loudest average. For a printer in a bedroom, the CC2 is the safer bet. If you buy the {buy:flashforge-adventurer-5m-pro}, set it to low-noise mode and schedule long prints for when the room is empty.

No named reviewer has published a decibel reading for the Toybox Alpha Four, so it isn't in the table. What Toybox does publish: the bed is unheated, the printer joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only, and setup links it to a Toybox account online. Toybox's help center says any third-party 1.75 mm PLA works and 'will not void your warranty', though it warns against glitter-filled filament. Toybox's own Printer Food costs $65 for four 500 g rolls, which is $32.50/kg.

Not recommended

Flashforge Adventurer 5M as the enclosed option. Its store listing mentions a 'fully enclosed print chamber', yet Flashforge sells a $39.99 enclosure kit for it, and the printer itself is open. Igor's Lab measured 62.3 dB(A) while printing, louder than the open A1 mini's 55.3 dB(A). If you want an enclosed printer, the 5M Pro or the Centauri Carbon 2 comes enclosed.
